new_findings.title: Missing admission can strand accepted GPU demand
new_findings.defect: The multipart route runs `await _accept_operation(...)` before `async with _maybe_admit_usage(...)` (describe.py:1476-1487). For GPU requests, repository line 113 creates `state=State.ACTIVE`, then the missing-service check raises 503 before the route's cleanup handlers are entered; repository line 186 renews `lease.expires_at` on same-key retries. Repeated failing retries can therefore keep consuming GPU demand capacity without dispatching compute.
new_findings.failure_scenario: A GPU multipart request has a database session but no usage-admission service: `_accept_operation` commits its ACTIVE demand lease, then admission returns 503. Retrying with the same operation_id renews the lease on each attempt and can exclude real GPU work from active-demand capacity.
new_findings.fix: Validate the metered admission service before accepting the operation, or terminalize the accepted GPU operation whenever admission setup fails. Add a database-backed regression asserting the lease is not ACTIVE after a missing-service 503 and remains released after a same-key retry.

summary: Both listed scene corrections are present with guard assertions, and one medium GPU demand-lease leak remains when admission is absent; lane verification hit the sandbox async SQLite timeout before producing a final summary.
